method.decision: Keep the strongest range in each view. Evaluate 0.30 interval IoU and 50% edit coverage and count additional range flags separately on each control. The range describes a temporary change in the recorded stereo field.
method.measurement: On 80 ms Hann windows every 20 ms, band-limit both channels to 300–2400 Hz. In each frame measure the strongest positive normalized cross-correlation at lags −16 through +16 samples, and the signed left/right RMS level ratio. Aggregate median lag, level and correlation over each 100 ms cell, using only energetic positively coherent frames.
method.return: Scan 0.7, 0.9 and 1.1 second candidate intervals on the 100 ms grid. Require matching five-cell flanks on both sides, with a one-cell guard. Compare the inside against both flanks; subtract any inside fluctuation beyond the flanks and half the flank distance. Compare level alone and equal-unit delay, level and correlation distance. Fit both points to the strict maximum of eligible unedited, room-only and same-path ordinary development views, including all noise levels.
method.sources: Use previously licensed and analyzed speech from separate reader groups. Author new matched path interventions using pinned Surrey and BBC measured stereo responses. Match ordinary and published synthetic donor durations and local gain, apply the same 20 ms fades, and reuse each background segment, level, and peak gain across versions. Include unchanged, masker-only, ordinary same-path and ordinary gradual-move controls. Synthetic and ordinary wrong-path inserts are both localization positives. Same-path synthetic inserts are separately reported as coverage probes, with no origin inference from this cue.
